title: Spring Is When Territory Decisions Are Made — The Season That Determines Your Year
content:
**The Season That Sets the Year** 

Spring is when homeowners in Wilmette, Highland Park, and the Lake Country corridor make their home decisions: the roof inspection after winter, the landscaping refresh, the HVAC tune-up before summer. It is also when contractors make the decision that determines their year — where, and whether, to build territory presence.

**The Compounding Math of Starting Now** 

Territory presence compounds. A contractor who starts structured neighborhood outreach in April has six months of accumulated recognition by October. A contractor who waits until July has three. The difference is not 50 percent — it is categorical, because recognition crosses a threshold where the brand becomes the default rather than an option.

**What Waiting Actually Costs** 

The cost of waiting is not just lost months. Under the SIT GroundForce™ model — one approved partner per industry per territory — waiting carries a second risk: the territory itself. When a roofing category closes in Winnetka or an HVAC category closes in Waukesha County, it closes for the duration of the active partner's agreement. 

The contractor who evaluates in spring and decides in fall may find the decision has been made for them. 

**Confirming Availability Takes Minutes** 

A territory review confirms whether your trade category is still open in your specific ZIP codes. Standard Review is free and processed in order received. Priority Territory Review is $99, includes a Territory Availability Summary within 48 hours, and is fully refunded if your territory is unavailable.
